rows.source_name: American Welding Society (AWS) Idaho/Montana Section Scholarships

fields.Due Date: Annual — opens Dec 1, closes Mar 1 (for the following fall term)
fields.Scholarship Location/Information: Regional — students in Idaho or Montana; AWS Idaho/Montana Section
fields.Name of Scholarship: American Welding Society (AWS) Idaho/Montana Section Scholarships
fields.Summary: The AWS Idaho/Montana Section funds welding/trades students in ID or MT pursuing a welding degree or certificate at a 2-year or 4-year school. A graduating Whitefish senior qualifies as an incoming welding student (AWS requires HS graduate/GED status by the fall term). One AWS Foundation online application at scholarship.aws.org covers National, District, and Section awards.

rows.source_name: Lineman Country Scholarship (Southeast Lineman Training Center)

fields.Scholarship Location/Information: National; Southeast Lineman Training Center (SLTC), Trenton, GA
fields.Name of Scholarship: Lineman Country Scholarship (Southeast Lineman Training Center)
fields.Summary: This trades/lineman scholarship from Southeast Lineman Training Center awards $5,000 (five awards in 2026) to individuals starting a career in the electrical utility/communications lineworker industry. A graduating high school senior or GED holder planning a lineman career qualifies; applicants submit letters of recommendation from three references and an essay to the Scholarship Committee.

fields.Amount: Varies (set yearly by the ILRA Board; covers tuition, textbooks, fees)
fields.Summary: This lineman/trades scholarship is for a son or daughter of a Journeyman Lineman OR someone recommended by one, entering accredited lineman training. Applicants need a high school diploma or GED, so a graduating Whitefish senior qualifies via the family/sponsor connection. Two recommendation letters (one from a HS/GED advisor) and a personal financial-need statement are required.

fields.Due Date: Annual — opens Dec 1, closes Jan 31 (11:59pm CST)
fields.Scholarship Location/Information: National; open to Eagle Scouts nationwide
fields.Summary: NESA scholarships are for Eagle Scouts and require NESA membership. They explicitly open to graduating high school seniors: Eagle Scouts may apply beginning in their senior year of high school. Awards range from a $5,000 Tappan Scholarship up to a $50,000 four-year Cooke Scholarship ($12,500/yr), with a hard filter on Eagle Scout / Scouting status.

rows.source_name: Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition (Grand Teton Music Festival)

fields.Due Date: Annual — spring (2026 deadline extended to Mon May 18)
fields.Scholarship Location/Information: Regional — Wyoming, Idaho, and Montana residents; competition held in Jackson, WY
fields.Name of Scholarship: Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition (Grand Teton Music Festival)
fields.Summary: The Donald Runnicles Musical Arts Scholarship Competition is a regional music award open to graduating high school seniors from Wyoming, Idaho or Montana who are pursuing a music degree in college. Montana is explicitly included, so a Whitefish HS senior planning a music degree fits. Selection is by video pre-screen then live semi-final/final rounds, with prizes of $10,000–$25,000.

rows.source_name: ESA Foundation Computer & Video Game Arts Scholarship

fields.Due Date: Annual — opens Apr 1, closes Apr 30 (11:59 PT)
fields.Scholarship Location/Information: National (US citizens); administered via Kaleidoscope online portal
fields.Name of Scholarship: ESA Foundation Computer & Video Game Arts Scholarship
fields.Summary: For students pursuing video-game, interactive-entertainment and STEAM careers, this esports/gaming award supports future game creators. Applicants may be graduating HS seniors entering a four-year undergraduate program in fall 2026. Priority to women, nonbinary/gender-nonconforming, or economically disadvantaged applicants.
fields.Focus: Video game arts / STEAM / interactive entertainment

fields.Due Date: Annual — opens Apr 1, closes Apr 30 (11:59 PT)
fields.Scholarship Location/Information: National (US citizens); administered via Kaleidoscope online portal
fields.Summary: This esports award supports students competing on or managing a college esports team/club, or those confirmed to compete at the collegiate level in fall 2026. A graduating HS senior can qualify if they are confirmed to compete on a college esports team in fall 2026 (a self-selected filter, not an ineligibility bar). Full-time four-year undergraduate enrollment, min 2.5 GPA, US citizenship, and financial need apply.

fields.Scholarship Location/Information: National (US high school seniors); mail/email application to VRG, Baltimore, MD
fields.Summary: The Vegetarian Resource Group awards students graduating from US high schools who have promoted vegetarianism/veganism in their schools and communities. This vegetarian/vegan-focused award grants one $10,000 and five $5,000 scholarships. Requires transcripts, three-plus recommendation letters, and an essay on advocacy and goals.

rows.source_name: Duck Brand "Stuck at Prom" Scholarship Contest

fields.Due Date: Annual — submit by early June (2026: Jun 3, 12 PM ET)
fields.Scholarship Location/Information: National (US, DC, PR, territories; excludes MD, CO, NE, ND — Montana eligible)
fields.Name of Scholarship: Duck Brand "Stuck at Prom" Scholarship Contest
fields.Summary: This creative/contest scholarship is a photo CONTEST, not a traditional essay scholarship: entrants make and wear original promwear from Duck Tape and submit a photo, judged on creativity and execution. Open to students 14+ enrolled at the high-school level during the 2025-2026 school year. Grand prizes are $10,000 per category with $1,000 runner-up and special-category awards.

fields.Due Date: Annual — closes Feb 14 (not shown on live portal page)
fields.Summary: A single Kaleidoscope portal application covering all Montana 4-H Foundation scholarships for Montana students with 4-H involvement (typically 3+ years in 4-H). 4-H membership is the gating criterion. Applicants complete one application and are matched to the scholarships they qualify for; graduating high school seniors are eligible.

fields.Due Date: Varies (most due senior year of HS, Dec–Apr)
fields.Scholarship Location/Information: National; online portal (futures.pearson.com/scholarships) aggregating FIRST partner scholarships
fields.Summary: The FIRST Scholarship program is a robotics/FIRST portal (hosted on Pearson Futures) linking graduating high school seniors who did FRC/FTC/FLL to 150+ partner scholarships from colleges, businesses, and associations. It is a dynamic portal, not a single award: each scholarship has its own amount, eligibility, process, and deadline. HS seniors are explicitly the target audience.

fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26GBBS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/gbci-leadership-scholarship
fields.Summary: For children, step-children, and employees of Glacier Bancorp (GBCI, headquartered in Kalispell, MT); full- or part-time students eligible. Corporate-sponsor employee/dependent scholarship. Typical award $2,000 per year.

rows.source_name: Dearborn Ranch Montana Game Wardens Scholarship

fields.Name of Scholarship: Dearborn Ranch Montana Game Wardens Scholarship
fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26DRSFGW) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/dearborn-ranch-montana-game-wardens-scholarship
fields.Summary: For biological or adopted children of active uniformed Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks Game Wardens (a law-enforcement / first responder family scholarship). Typical award $10,000 per year.

rows.source_name: Dearborn Ranch Montana Highway Patrol Scholarship

fields.Name of Scholarship: Dearborn Ranch Montana Highway Patrol Scholarship
fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26DRSFHP) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/dearborn-ranch-montana-highway-patrol-scholarship
fields.Summary: For biological or adopted children of active uniformed Montana Highway Patrol officers (a first responder / law-enforcement family scholarship). Minimum cumulative GPA 2.75. Award $10,000 per year.

fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26KMSE) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/kay-mcmillan-nursing-scholarship
fields.Summary: For graduating seniors enrolling in the pre-nursing program at Montana Tech (or current Montana Tech pre-nursing / nursing students) who show a commitment to community health. Minimum high-school GPA 2.0. Typical award $500–$1,500 per year. Nursing / healthcare focus.

fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26BLAK) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/alan-and-janette-blackburn-scholarship
fields.Summary: Open to any student who graduated or will graduate from a Montana high school, awarded through the Montana Community Foundation. Typical award $500–$1,000 per year. Applies to Whitefish, MT graduating seniors statewide.

rows.source_name: Nep & Mary Ellen Lynch Trade School Scholarship

fields.Name of Scholarship: Nep & Mary Ellen Lynch Trade School Scholarship
fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26NMES) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/nep-mary-ellen-lynch-trade-school-scholarship
fields.Summary: For current graduating seniors and past graduates of Montana high schools enrolling full- or part-time at an accredited Montana trade school (cosmetology and massage schools are ineligible). Trade / vocational focus. Typical award $5,000 per year.

rows.source_name: T. Eugene Young Montana's Promise Scholarship

fields.Name of Scholarship: T. Eugene Young Montana's Promise Scholarship
fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26TEYS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/t-eugene-young-montanas-promise-scholarship
fields.Summary: For graduating Montana high school seniors pursuing STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) or healthcare degrees to strengthen Montana's workforce. Typical award $1,000–$1,500 per year.

rows.source_name: Reach for the Future Scholarship for Vocational Degree Programs

fields.Name of Scholarship: Reach for the Future Scholarship for Vocational Degree Programs
fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26VMSE2YR) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/reach-for-the-future-scholarship-for-vocational-degree-programs
fields.Summary: For Montana residents (or those with strong Montana ties) enrolled — or seeking enrollment — full-time at a public, private, or tribal college in Montana, studying a vocational or trade program such as aviation technology, carpentry, welding, automobile mechanics, or plumbing. Financial need required. Two-year renewable award, $2,500 per year (must maintain a 2.5 GPA to renew).
fields.Focus: Vocational, Trades (welding, aviation technology, carpentry, plumbing)

fields.Application Link/Method: Apply via the MCF Scholarship Portal (Access Code 26GOMS) — https://mtcf.org/scholarship/gary-olszewski-memorial-scholarship
fields.Summary: For students enrolling in a two-year technical / trade program at an accredited school; honors a Montana dryland farmer-tradesman to encourage careers in the trades (carpentry, plumbing, electrical, mechanics). Typical award $8,000 per year for two years. Open statewide, with a preference for Blaine/Hill/Phillips County students.

fields.Amount: $5,000/year, renewable up to 4 years ($20,000 total); up to 100 awards
fields.Summary: National merit scholarship from Equitable (administered by Scholarship America) for U.S. high school seniors with a 2.5+ GPA planning full-time enrollment in a two- or four-year college. $5,000 per year, renewable up to four years ($20,000 total); up to 100 awards. Annual cycle typically opens September and closes December.

fields.Amount: Minimum five awards of $1,000 each (per student)
fields.Summary: National NAEHCY Scholar Fund award for students who are or have been homeless and are McKinney-Vento eligible. Open to college-bound graduating seniors and postsecondary students under 23; a minimum of five $1,000 awards, usable at any accredited U.S. college. 2026 deadline July 31 (recurs annually).
